findings.evidence: Write to the requested path; else next to the user's existing deck, else a workspace path such as `slides/<topic>.md`. ... If writing is impossible, return the Markdown inline and never claim a save.
findings.fix: Cut the Save section to one line: "Use `/mnt/user-data/outputs/` only if it exists; report whether the deck was rendered or only linted." The model already knows the rest of the path fallback order and not to claim a save it did not make.

findings.evidence: Apply the smallest fix per defect: split a dense slide, shorten a heading, repair a directive, or swap in one template's `<style>` block when the colors themselves are the problem.
findings.fix: Add a decision rule for when to keep the user's own CSS and when to replace it with a template style block. For example: keep the user's CSS when it defines classes the deck uses; when you swap, carry over every `section.<class>` the deck references so no `_class` directive is left without a rule.

findings.evidence: "Content headings are concise and slides have at most five bullets each."
findings.fix: Make the check measurable, for example "Every `##` heading is at most 45 characters and no slide has more than five bullets". Also drop `assets/template-tech.md` from `files` in precise-slides, because it is a skill asset and not a user input file.

findings.evidence: gradient | `template-gradient.md` | visual keynote, little text | dark gradient; `<!-- _class: warm -->` or `teal` per slide
findings.fix: Add to the gradient row or to Gotchas: "`_class` replaces classes. To use a variant on a title or divider slide, write `<!-- _class: lead warm -->`. A bare `warm` drops `lead` and loses the centering." Today this only appears in references/marp-syntax.md, which the gradient path does not load.
